title: Which order to lay two shadow tones (demo)
question: When shading with two tones, is it better to lay the dark one or the light one first?
stopped: Every needed claim has a location in a source (a demo, so only two sources)

claims.claim: Laying the dark tone first keeps the boundary from getting muddy
claims.note: Appears in both a personal record and a paper.

quotes.text: わたしは影を塗るとき、まず一番暗い色を先に置く。 明るい影から置くと、あとで暗い影を重ねたときに境目が濁るからだ。
quotes.en: When I shade, I lay the darkest tone first. If I start with the light shadow, the boundary gets muddy when I layer the dark shadow over it later.

quotes.text: In 9 of 12 cases, placing the darkest tone first produced fewer visible seams at layer boundaries.

claims.note: One sentence in the paper. It doesn't say how much blending makes it disappear.

quotes.text: The effect disappeared when layers were blended with a soft brush.

disagreements.topic: Is the order reversed for watercolour?

quotes.text: ただし水彩の場合は逆で、明るい色から重ねるのが定石だと聞く。 自分は水彩を描かないので、ここは確かめていない。
quotes.en: With watercolour, though, I hear it's the other way round, and the standard is to layer from the light tones. I don't paint in watercolour, so I haven't checked this.
quotes.who: The writer of the sample post (hearsay)

unreached: A record of the writer themselves trying the watercolour order (not found; assumed for the demo)
